subject: Linguistics
title: Dialects and Accents
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dialects and Accents usable.

hook.text: A Texan, a Bostonian, and a Londoner all speak English—but sound worlds apart.

buildup.text: An accent is about pronunciation; a dialect includes different grammar and vocabulary too.

discovery.text: No dialect is linguistically 'better'—standard forms just have more political power.

twist.text: Every person actually speaks their own unique version called an idiolect.

climax.text: Dialects form along geography, class, ethnicity, and age—they map social identity.

punchline.text: Your dialect is your linguistic fingerprint.

quiz.question: What is the difference between an accent and a dialect?
options: Accent is pronunciation only; dialect includes grammar
